learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the different tools, mediums, and surfaces artists use to bring their creative visions to life!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A medium refers to the materials used to create an artwork. Dry mediums include pencils, charcoal, and pastels. Wet mediums include watercolors, acrylics, and oil paints.
A transparent painting medium where pigments are mixed with water. It is known for its light, airy feel. The white of the paper is used to create highlights.
Acrylic paints dry very quickly and are water-soluble when wet but water-resistant when dry. Oil paints dry very slowly, allowing artists to blend colors smoothly over days.
Brushes come in different shapes: round (for details), flat (for broad strokes), and filbert (for blending). Artists also use palette knives to apply thick layers of paint (impasto).
Paintings can be done on paper, canvas, or wood. Canvases are usually treated with a primer called 'Gesso' to prevent the paint from soaking into the fabric.

fun_activity.title: ☕ Coffee Painting
fun_activity.instructions: You don't need fancy paints to be an artist! Mix instant coffee powder with a few drops of water to create a dark brown 'paint'. Add more water to create lighter shades. Paint a beautiful sepia-toned landscape!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Watercolors (transparent, quick-drying) and Oil paints (opaque, slow-drying).
📌 Know the purpose of a primer/gesso (it prepares the canvas surface for painting).
📌 Identify basic brush shapes: Round, Flat, and Filbert.
quick_recap: ⭐ Pigments are the colored powders that give paint its hue.
⭐ Dry pastels act like chalk, while oil pastels have a waxy, buttery consistency.
⭐ Acrylics are popular because they are versatile, dry fast, and can mimic both watercolors and oils.
